prompt: Hey, we've got to decide on the cold-chain thing. The board wants a 3% spoilage reduction this year. Option A is upgrading sensors at all 40 stores, that's $210K. Option B is the new forecasting tool, $180K. I'm not leaning either way honestly, both have merit. The sensor upgrade is proven tech, but installation will disrupt store ops for like 2 weeks. The forecasting tool is software, faster to roll out, but it depends on our data quality which has been spotty. We have the budget for one, not both. Need to give the VP of Operations a recommendation by Friday. What do you think? Also, the sensor vendor said they can start next month, but the tool needs a 6-week integration. Let me know what you'd present.

Need to make a call on the ERP vs custom integration. We have a $3M capex cap. Option A is the ERP module upgrade, $1.2M, payback in 14 months. Option B is a custom integration, $900K, payback in 10 months. I'm leaning A because the ERP is a long-term strategic play, even though it's pricier. The custom integration is cheaper and faster payback, but it's a band-aid. The CFO will sign off on one. We have to present by next week. Also, the ERP vendor says we need a dedicated team for 3 months. The custom one we can do with our existing staff. What's your take? I want to make sure I'm not missing any hidden costs.

We have this false-alarm bug with the sensors. Option A is a hardware redesign, $75K, fixes it for good. Option B is a software patch, $45K, but there's a 30% residual-risk rate that false alarms could still happen. I'm leaning B because it's cheaper and faster, and we can monitor it. The Head of Product needs to decide. We have a Q3 launch deadline. The hardware redesign takes 4 months, the patch can ship in 6 weeks. Also, the hardware would require a recall of existing units, which is a logistic nightmare. What's your suggestion? We need to present a clear recommendation.

We're doing a Q4 retention push. Need to pick a tool. Option A is a $95K annual survey platform, it's pretty standard. Option B is a $140K engagement analytics suite with AI-driven insights. I have no strong lean. The survey platform is cheaper and easy to deploy, but the analytics suite gives deeper data. The Director of HR will decide. We have a 2,000-person company. The analytics suite has a 3-month implementation, the survey platform can go live in 2 weeks. Also, the analytics suite requires integration with our HRIS, which might be a pain. What do you recommend? I need to send a summary to the Director by end of day.

Security audit flagged some gaps. We need to decide on a solution. Option A is a managed SIEM, $60K/year. Option B is building in-house detection, $150K over 6 months. I'm not leaning either way. The managed SIEM is quick to deploy, but ongoing cost. In-house is a big upfront investment, but we own it. The CTO will make the call. We have a compliance deadline in 9 months. Also, the managed SIEM vendor says they can have us live in 4 weeks. In-house would take the full 6 months. What's your take? We need a recommendation for the CTO.

We have a $5M budget cap for fuel efficiency. Option A is a fleet retrofit, $4.2M, saves 7% fuel. Option B is route-optimization software, $3.8M, saves 5%. I'm leaning A because the retrofit is a physical asset improvement, more durable. The software is cheaper but might have ongoing licensing. The GM needs to decide. We have 12 aircraft in the fleet. The retrofit takes 2 months per plane, so about 6 months total. The software can be deployed in 8 weeks. Also, the retrofit has a 10-year lifespan, the software needs renewal every year. What do you think? I need to present a clear option.

We need to close a $1.5M pipeline by year-end. Option A is expanding the inside-sales team, $25K/month. Option B is hiring an enterprise account manager, $40K/month. I'm leaning B because we need to focus on large deals. The VP of Sales will decide. The inside-sales team can handle more volume, but the enterprise AM can build relationships. We have 4 months left. The inside-sales expansion can start in 2 weeks, the AM hire might take 6 weeks to find. Also, the AM would need a higher commission structure. What's your recommendation? I want to make sure we hit the number.

We need to cut delivery times by 20%. Option A is a warehouse automation pilot at one site, $500K. Option B is a last-mile delivery partnership trial, $350K. I have no lean. The warehouse automation is a big investment but could scale. The delivery partnership is cheaper but might not be as reliable. The Head of Supply Chain needs to decide. We have 5 warehouses. The pilot would take 3 months to set up. The partnership trial can start in 1 month. Also, the automation vendor says we need to train staff, which is extra cost. What's your take? I need to present both options clearly.

We have a $150K budget and a security mandate. Option A is an on-prem data-center refresh, $120K. Option B is a cloud migration, $100K/year with a 2-year break-even. I'm leaning B because it's more scalable and we don't have to manage hardware. The Director of IT will decide. We have a compliance requirement to meet. The on-prem refresh takes 3 months, the cloud migration takes 6 months. Also, the cloud has ongoing costs, but we can scale down. What do you think? I need to send a recommendation to the Director by tomorrow.

We have Q3 targets to hit. Option A is a chatbot upgrade, $80K, deflects 15% more tickets. Option B is a proactive-outreach program, $60K, cuts churn by 5%. I have no lean. The chatbot is a tech fix, the outreach is more personal. The VP of Customer Success needs to decide. We have a customer base of 50K. The chatbot upgrade can be done in 4 weeks. The outreach program needs a team of 2 for 3 months. Also, the outreach might increase response times. What's your suggestion? I need to present a clear option to the VP.

Need a message to our COO, Maria, about a decision. We have to pick between an EHR upgrade at $450K or a patient-scheduling AI tool at $300K. Goal is to cut no-shows by 10%. The EHR upgrade is more comprehensive, takes 4 months, integrates with existing systems. The AI tool is cheaper, faster (2 months), but it's a new vendor, unknown integration issues. I'm leaning towards the EHR upgrade honestly, seems more reliable long-term, but the cost is high. We have to decide by Friday. Also, we don't know if the AI tool can handle our patient volume during peak hours, that's a question mark. Write a message to Maria with the details, my lean, and ask her to choose. Keep it professional.

Hey, drafting a note for our Head of Marketing, Priya. We have a budget of $180K for a growth initiative. Option 1 is an influencer campaign, projected cost $150K, with a 12% ROAS. It's trendy, quick to set up, but the ROI is a bit uncertain. Option 2 is a full SEO overhaul, $200K, which is over budget, but projected ROAS is 15%. We might need to find extra $20K. I'm leaning towards the SEO overhaul because it's more sustainable long-term, even though it costs more. But the influencer campaign is cheaper and might get quicker wins. Priya needs to decide which one to fund, and also if we should stretch the budget. We have to present this in the Monday meeting. Can you draft the message? Also, we haven't picked specific influencers yet, that's a big unknown.

We need to decide on infrastructure vs engine optimization for the game. Server upgrade is $250K, engine optimization is $180K. Both should cut load times by 30% before Q4 launch. The server upgrade is more reliable, but the engine work is cheaper and might have better long-term performance. I don't have a strong preference, but we need to pick one by end of week. The team is split. We have the budget for either, but not both. The concern with the engine optimization is it might introduce new bugs, and we haven't tested it on the new maps yet. The server upgrade is more straightforward but takes longer to deploy. Need a message to our Director of Engineering, Ravi, laying out the trade-offs. Ask him to make the call. Include the costs and the load time target.

Hi, need to send a decision request to our VP of Logistics, Sarah. We're looking at route-planning software at $600K vs a fleet-tracking hardware rollout at $750K. Both could cut fuel costs by 8%. The software is cheaper and easier to implement, but the hardware gives us real-time data that could be useful later. The hardware rollout is a bigger upfront investment and takes longer to install across the fleet. We haven't decided on a vendor for either, and we need to factor in maintenance costs. We have a board meeting in 3 weeks, so need a decision soon. Can you draft a message for Sarah with the options, costs, and the fuel savings target? No lean from me, just present the facts and ask her to choose.

We're a food bank and we're seeing a 20% surge in demand expected this winter. We need to pick a tool to handle it. Option A is a donation-management system, $40K. Option B is a volunteer-scheduling tool, $55K. The donation system would help us track incoming food and funds better, which is critical right now. The volunteer tool would help us coordinate the extra volunteers we'll need. I'm leaning towards A because donations are our lifeline, but B is also important. We have a limited budget, maybe enough for one. Our CFO, David, needs to approve the spend. We need to act fast, like within the next 2 weeks. Can you write a message to David outlining both options, costs, and my lean, and ask for his approval? Also, we haven't calculated the exact cost of the demand surge, that's an unknown.

We need to accelerate our clinical trial by 3 months. Two options: buy new lab equipment for $2M or invest in a data-analysis platform for $1.5M. The lab equipment would speed up sample processing, the data platform would speed up our analysis of results. I'm leaning towards the data platform because we can process our existing data faster, and it's cheaper. But the lab equipment is a physical asset that might have more long-term value. We have to present to our Head of R&D, Dr. Chen, by next Thursday. We need a decision on which to fund. Also, we're not sure if the data platform can integrate with our current systems, that's a risk. Can you draft a message to Dr. Chen with the costs, the 3-month goal, and my lean towards B, asking for a decision?

We have a $300K sustainability budget for our hotels. Two projects: HVAC retrofit at $350K, which is over budget, but saves 15% energy. Or solar panel install at $280K, under budget, saves 10%. We might be able to get extra funds for the HVAC, but it's not guaranteed. The solar panels have a longer payback period. I don't have a strong preference, but we need to present a recommendation to our Director of Facilities, Tom. He needs to decide which to fund, and if we should request more budget. We have a quarterly review in 2 weeks. Also, we haven't assessed the condition of all our roofs for the solar panels, that's a big unknown. Write a message to Tom with the options, costs, savings, and ask him to choose.

We're trying to boost our conversion rate from 2% to 4%. Two ideas: a customer-reference program for $120K, or a sales-demo automation tool for $90K. The reference program would leverage our happy customers, but it takes time to build. The demo automation would speed up our sales cycle, but it's a tool that needs setup. We have the budget for one, maybe both if we cut elsewhere. Our CEO, Alex, needs to decide on the priority. We need to show progress in the next quarter. I don't have a strong lean, but the demo tool is cheaper. Also, we don't know how many customers would actually participate in the reference program, that's a big unknown. Can you draft a message to Alex with the costs, the conversion goal, and ask for a decision?

We have a regulatory deadline in 6 months. We need to fix our data issues. Option A is a data-governance tool at $450K, which helps with policies and compliance. Option B is a data-quality fix at $300K, which cleans up our existing data. I'm leaning towards A because it's more comprehensive and prevents future issues. But B is cheaper and might be quicker to implement. We need to present to our VP of Data, Rachel, and get her approval. We have to start soon to meet the deadline. Also, we haven't audited our data to know the full scope of the problem, that's a risk. Write a message to Rachel with the options, costs, the 6-month deadline, and my lean, asking her to choose.

We need to improve driver retention by 8%. Two options: a driver-incentive program for $200K, or a surge-pricing algorithm update for $150K. The incentive program is direct, gives drivers bonuses. The algorithm update would make surges more frequent, increasing earnings. We have to decide which to implement. Our Head of Operations, Lisa, needs to approve. We have a driver feedback survey coming in next week that might inform the decision, but we need to move fast. I don't have a lean, but the algorithm is cheaper. Also, we don't know the exact impact of the algorithm on rider demand, that's a risk. Can you draft a message to Lisa with the costs, the 8% goal, and ask for a decision? Include the survey timing.

Hey, need your take on this. We have to decide on our raw material sourcing for next year. Option A is switching to a new supplier, it's a $1M upfront investment but gives us a 10% cost cut. Option B is renegotiating our current long-term contract, that's $800K and a 7% cut. We're looking at a 12-month horizon to see the savings. I'm leaning towards B because it's less disruptive to our existing supply chain, but I'm open to being convinced otherwise. The final call is yours, we need to move by end of quarter. Also, I haven't figured out the switching costs for A beyond the initial investment, like potential downtime during the transition. Can you put together a clear summary for me to present to the Director of Procurement? She needs to approve the budget and pick one.

We need to decide on our next feature investment to hit that 10% weekly active user growth target. Option 1 is a podcast feature, $100K to build. Option 2 is a playlist personalization upgrade, $80K. I don't have a strong opinion yet, both seem viable. The podcast thing could bring in new users, but personalization might keep existing ones more engaged. We have to pick one by next sprint planning. I'm not sure which has better long-term retention, and we haven't measured the impact of either on churn. The VP of Product will make the final decision, she needs a clear comparison of costs, timelines, and expected impact on that metric. Also, do we have any data on what our users are actually asking for? I don't have that handy. Get me a summary I can forward.

Critical decision coming up. We need to be FedRAMP compliant in 9 months. Option A is a zero-trust architecture pilot, $250K. Option B is an endpoint detection and response upgrade, $180K. I'm leaning towards A because it's a more fundamental fix, but B might be quicker to implement. The CISO will sign off, she needs to see the risk reduction each offers against the compliance requirements. I don't know the exact timeline for A, it might take longer than 9 months to fully deploy. Also, the vendor for B has a patch schedule that might not align with our deadline. Can you draft a decision brief for her? Include the costs, the compliance gaps each addresses, and the open questions on timing.

We have to fix our order error problem and speed up service. Two options on the table. Option 1 is a POS system upgrade, that's $300K. Option 2 is a delivery app integration, $250K. We want to cut order errors by 15% and shave time off each transaction. I have no lean here, the ops team is split. The COO wants a recommendation-ready summary by Friday. I don't have the failure rates for the current POS, and the delivery app integration depends on a third-party API that might have latency issues. Also, training costs for the POS upgrade aren't fully known. Put together a comparison for the COO, she'll decide the budget allocation. Make sure to highlight the unknowns, especially the API reliability and the training overhead.

Status update for the director of engineering. Print farm uptime is at 94% over the last two weeks, which is good. But the new ceramic material profile is still failing calibration on two of the twelve printers. We suspect a firmware mismatch with the latest slicer update. We haven't confirmed that yet, and we don't have a workaround. The two affected printers are down for ceramic jobs, so we're rerouting to others, but that's adding latency. We're tracking this daily. We have a ticket open with the slicer vendor, but no ETA. No decision needed from you right now, just keeping you in the loop. We'll escalate if it doesn't resolve by the end of the week. Also, the other ten printers are running fine with the standard materials.

Quick status for the head of sustainability. The closed-loop dye-water recycling pilot at the main plant is cutting water usage by 18%, which is on track. However, the membrane filters are clogging way faster than the vendor said they would. We're replacing them twice as often as spec, and that's eating into the savings. We don't know the long-term replacement cost for a full rollout yet, that's the big unknown. We're collecting data on the clogging rate to estimate it. No action needed from you now, just wanted you to have the numbers. We'll have a cost projection in about two weeks. The pilot is still running, and we're not pausing it. Just flagging the risk.

Status for the VP of engineering. The new orthorectification pipeline is processing 40% more scenes per day, great improvement. But the atmospheric correction step is creating a color-shift artifact on images over snow-covered terrain. It's not affecting the geometric accuracy, but it makes the imagery look off. The fix is unestimated right now, we haven't scoped it. We have a couple of workarounds, like running a different correction for those scenes, but that adds manual review time. We're tracking the number of affected scenes, about 5% of the daily volume. No decision needed from you yet, just informing. We'll open a ticket and estimate the fix next sprint. If it gets worse, we might need to pause that step, but we're not there yet.

Update for the lead data scientist. The new predictive ETAs are 12% more accurate on the southern corridor, so that's a win. But the model's confidence drops sharply for trains carrying oversized loads, like heavy machinery or large transformers. We don't have enough retraining data for that segment, it's incomplete. We have maybe 200 historical trips with oversized loads, but they're all from one season, so not diverse. We're trying to get more data from other corridors, but that's slow. No decision needed from you right now, just want to flag it. We're going to try to augment the data with synthetic samples, but that has its own risks. We'll keep you posted on the accuracy for that segment.

Status for the director of IT. The unified patient portal app is now rolled out to 78% of our clinics, that's 34 out of 43. The remaining ones are on track for next month. However, the single sign-on integration with the legacy radiology system is still failing. It's not blocking the rollout, but it's causing complaints from clinicians who have to log in twice. The vendor hasn't given us a patch timeline, that's unknown. We've escalated it, but no date yet. No decision needed from you, just an update. We're considering a temporary workaround, but we want to wait for the vendor's patch first. If it drags past two weeks, we might have to implement something interim.

Heads up for the head of fleet operations. The new battery-swapping route in the downtown pilot cut downtime by 22%, so that's working. But we're running low on swappable batteries because the charging depot staff are on a holiday schedule, so they're not charging them as fast. The reorder lead time for new batteries is a blocker, it's like 6 weeks. We have enough for maybe 3 more days at the current rate. We're trying to shift staff from other depots, but they're also short. No decision needed from you right now, just letting you know. We might have to reduce the pilot scope temporarily if we can't get more batteries. We're monitoring it daily and will escalate if it becomes critical.

Hey, we need a status update for our CTO, Priya. The new e-discovery search index is live and it's fast—under 2 seconds on most queries. But we've got a nasty issue: the date-range filter times out on really large custodial sets, like 100k+ documents. Performance team is still triaging it, no ETA yet. We're at 85% of our Q3 perf targets without that fixed. Also, the new index is using about 1.2TB of storage, which is under the 1.5TB we budgeted, so that's good. The timeout only happens on the biggest matters, but one of our top 10 clients has one of those. We're not asking her to decide anything, just want her to know we're on it. We'll have the triage result by Friday. She reads this before our weekly sync. Can you draft a short status she can skim in a minute? Thanks.

We need a status update for our program manager at the water utility, Ravi. Smart-meter rollout is at 1,200 out of 5,000 targeted homes, so about 24%. We're behind schedule by 2 weeks because of permitting delays in the older neighborhoods. The mesh network is dropping packets in those areas—about 5% packet loss, which is way above our 1% target. We think it's because of the thick walls and old infrastructure, but we're not sure. We've got a repeater placement plan, but it's awaiting budget approval—$50k for 40 repeaters. We're hoping to get approval next week. We're not asking Ravi to decide anything, just want him to know where we stand. We'll have more data after we test the repeaters in one neighborhood. Can you write a status update for him? He'll read it before the board meeting.

Status update for our product lead, Jane. The new safety-certified torque sensor is passing all lab tests—we've run 500+ test cycles with no issues. But the field beta units are reporting a firmware crash when the arm encounters a sudden stall. We've seen it on 3 out of 20 beta units. The crash log is still being analyzed, but we suspect a race condition in the control loop. We don't know the root cause yet. We've got a potential workaround that limits the torque spike, but it reduces responsiveness by 10%. We're not asking Jane to decide anything, just want her to know we're on it. We're aiming to have a fix by the end of the month, but that's tentative. The lab tests are all green, so the sensor itself is solid. Can you draft a status update for her?

Need a status update for our VP of operations, Marcus. The new automated pallet-mover fleet is handling 15% more moves per hour—up to 42 moves/hour from 36. That's great. But one unit is intermittently losing its location beacon in the freezer aisle. It happens about every 2 hours, lasts for 30 seconds, then it recovers. We don't know the interference source—could be the metal racks, the cold, or something else. We've checked the beacon signal strength, it's fine. We're not asking Marcus to decide anything, just want him to know we're aware and investigating. We've got a temp fix: we put a manual override in that aisle, but it adds 5 minutes per shift. We'll have a full analysis by next Tuesday. Can you write a status update for him?

Status update for our head of analytics, Sofia. The new in-play odds engine is improving profit margin by 0.4%—that's on top of the 1.2% we were already seeing. Good. But the model's performance degrades significantly during major live events, like the World Cup final or the Super Bowl. We saw a 15% drop in accuracy during the last big match. We think it's because of the massive spike in betting volume—we saw 10x normal traffic. The scaling plan for peak traffic is not yet finalized. We're looking at adding more compute nodes, but that's a cost decision. We're not asking Sofia to decide anything, just want her to know the status. We'll have a proposal by the end of the week. Can you draft a status update for her?

Hey, we need a status update for our director of engineering, Alex. The new RTL simulation cluster is running 30% faster—we're seeing 3.2x speedup on our standard testbench. But the license server for the verification tools is hitting its concurrency limit. We've got 200 licenses, but we're seeing 210 concurrent users during peak times. That's causing some jobs to queue and wait. The additional license cost is pending procurement—we need 50 more licenses at $10k each, so $500k. We're not asking Alex to decide anything, just want him to know we're aware and have a plan. We're hoping to get procurement approved by next week. We've also noticed that the cluster is using 5% more power than expected, but that's minor. Can you write a status update for him?

Status update for our GM, Elena. The new temperature-controlled shipping lane has reduced spoilage claims by 40%—we went from 50 claims per quarter to 30. That's a big win. But the insurance underwriter is now asking for a higher premium due to the perceived risk of the new packaging. They want to increase our premium by 15%, which would cost us an extra $120k per year. The renewal terms are unclear—they haven't given us a final quote yet. We're not asking Elena to decide anything, just want her to know the situation. We're negotiating with the underwriter to get a better rate, but we don't know if they'll budge. We'll have more info by next week. Can you draft a status update for her?

Need a status update for our VP of technology, Nina. The new mobile key feature is adopted by 60% of guests at the flagship property—that's 1,200 out of 2,000 guests last week. Good. But the Bluetooth handshake fails on a specific older phone model—the iPhone 8. We see about 10% of guests using that phone, and they can't unlock their doors. We've got a workaround: they can use the web app, but it's clunky. We're still testing the workaround to make sure it's reliable. We're not asking Nina to decide anything, just want her to know we're on it. We're aiming to have a fix by the end of the month. We've also got a 2% failure rate on other models, but that's within spec. Can you write a status update for her?

Status update for our lead engineer, Tom. The new battery-storage controller is balancing loads correctly—we've seen stable voltage across 10 installations. But the grid-tie inverter is tripping a fault when the local utility performs a rapid voltage sag. We've seen it happen 3 times in the last week. The ride-through settings are in question—we don't know if they're set correctly for the utility's requirements. We're waiting on the utility to provide their spec, but they've been slow. We're not asking Tom to decide anything, just want him to know the status. We've got a temporary fix: we can adjust the settings manually, but that requires a site visit. We'll have a more permanent solution once we get the spec. Can you draft a status update for him?

Hey, we need a status update for our director of product, Chris. The new ethnicity-estimate update is live for 90% of users—that's 900k out of 1M. Good. But a specific haplogroup—let's say H1—is now reporting a confidence interval that is too wide. We're seeing a 95% CI of +/- 15%, which is way too broad. The underlying algorithm tweak is unverified—we don't know if it's causing the issue. We're investigating, but we don't have a root cause yet. We're not asking Chris to decide anything, just want him to know we're aware. We're aiming to have a fix by the end of the week. We've also noticed that the overall accuracy is up by 2%, so it's a trade-off. Can you write a status update for him?

Hi, we need to send a status update to Dana, our head of logistics. The drone inventory audit is live at the main warehouse. It's cutting stock-counting time from 3 days to about 4 hours per cycle. Huge win. But there's a problem: the drone's camera fails to read barcodes in low-light conditions. The main warehouse has poor lighting on the north side, and that's where 40% of our inventory is. We tested it last week, and the read failure rate there is 1 in 5. The lighting upgrade to fix this would cost $15k, and it's not in this quarter's budget. We're not asking Dana to approve the spend right now, just to be aware. We think we can work around it by scheduling drone flights during daylight hours, but that might delay some counts by 2 days. Also, we haven't figured out if the low-light issue affects the secondary warehouse, which has skylights. We'll check that next week. Dana should just read this and know the status, no action needed unless she wants to flag it to finance.

Need to update Priya, our CFO, on the ad-tier performance. Quick status, no decision needed. We launched the ad-supported tier 6 weeks ago. Current numbers: ad revenue is $0.02 per user-hour. That's below our initial projection of $0.03. The cost of serving ad-supported streams is $0.01 higher per user-hour than the premium tier. Why? More ad insertion logic, more bandwidth for the same video quality, and some extra telemetry. So the margin per user-hour is negative. We're recalculating the break-even point now. The original model assumed we'd need $0.025 per user-hour to break even. We're not there yet. Also, the ad fill rate is at 75%, which is lower than the 90% we planned for. We don't know if that's seasonal or a targeting issue. We're testing a few fixes. Priya should just be aware of these numbers. We'll send a more detailed analysis with a recommendation in 2 weeks. No action needed from her right now.

PR for the orders table index migration. Reviewer: Ravi. Files changed: 3. Migration file, a new index definition, and a config change. Line counts: +120, -15. The migration adds a composite index on (customer_id, created_at) to speed up order history queries. We ran the test suite: 120 tests passing, 2 new tests added for the index behavior. One thing not tested: index size on disk. We didn't check how much space the new index takes up on a production-sized table. Our staging table is only 1 million rows, but production has 50 million. The index could be large. I'm not sure if that's a problem for our disk budget. Also, we didn't check the migration time on a large table. It might lock the table for a while. The migration is using a standard ALTER TABLE, which in Postgres can take a lock. We're not sure if that's acceptable. Ravi should review the migration and decide if we need to test the index size or use a different migration strategy. The PR is ready for his review.

PR description for the flaky retry-logic fix in the payments webhook. Reviewer: Alex. Files changed: 2. The webhook handler and a test file. Line counts: +80, -40. The issue was that retries were firing too aggressively, causing duplicate charge attempts. We fixed the retry logic to use exponential backoff with jitter. Tests: 45 passing, 3 new tests. The new tests cover retry timing and duplicate prevention. One thing untested: out-of-order event delivery. That's when a later event arrives before an earlier one. Our fix doesn't handle that case, and we didn't write a test for it. We're not sure if the payment provider can send events out of order. We've seen it happen once in staging, but not in production. Alex should review the fix and decide if we need to handle out-of-order events in this PR or file a follow-up. Also, the retry backoff now goes from 1 second to 5 minutes over 5 attempts. That seems reasonable, but we haven't tested the behavior under high load. The PR is ready.

PR for adding a caching layer to the session-store service. Reviewer: Sam. Files changed: 4. The cache implementation, a config file, the service main file, and a test file. Line counts: +200, -30. We added an in-memory cache in front of the session store. Latency dropped from 120ms to 30ms on the read path, which is a 75% improvement. The write path is unchanged at 100ms. We ran the test suite: all existing tests pass, plus 5 new tests for cache hit/miss behavior. One thing untested: cache-eviction race condition. That's when two requests try to evict and repopulate the same key at the same time. We didn't write a test for that. We think the code handles it with a mutex, but we're not 100% sure. Sam should review the eviction logic and decide if we need a test for the race condition or if the mutex is sufficient. Also, the cache size is set to 10,000 entries. We don't know if that's enough for peak traffic. We'll monitor. The PR is ready for review.

PR for upgrading the TLS library across all services. Reviewer: the security lead, Jordan. Files changed: 12. All service configs and the shared TLS setup. Line counts: +60, -50. We upgraded from TLS 1.2 to TLS 1.3 across all 12 services. Handshake time improved from 40ms to 25ms on average. That's a 37% reduction. We ran the full test suite: 230 tests passing, 0 new tests. The change is mostly config. One question for Jordan: there's a cipher suite deprecation. The old library supports TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA, but the new library marks it as deprecated. PR for adding a circuit breaker to the downstream inventory API. Reviewer: Chris. Files changed: 3. The circuit breaker class, the API client, and a test file. Line counts: +150, -20. The inventory API has been flaky, with error rates spiking to 15% during peak hours. We added a circuit breaker that opens after 5 consecutive failures and stays open for 30 seconds. During the open state, we return a cached response. Error rate dropped to 2% in our tests. We ran the test suite: 180 tests passing, 4 new tests for the circuit breaker. One thing untested: slow-response case. That's when the API responds slowly but doesn't error out. Our circuit breaker doesn't handle that. It only counts failures, not timeouts. We didn't test or implement a timeout-based trip. Chris should review and decide if we need to add a timeout-based circuit breaker in this PR or if the failure-based one is enough for now. Also, the cached response is from 5 minutes ago, which might be stale. We're not sure if that's acceptable. The PR is ready.
